title: Centre Defers Manipur Census Amid Protests Over NRC and Ethnic Tensions
excerpt: The September 1 house-listing exercise was put on hold after Amit Shah chaired a review and civil-society groups demanded an NRC update first.
body:
• The Centre has deferred census operations in Manipur after Home Minister Amit Shah chaired a review meeting
  • The proposed September 1 house-listing exercise was put on hold amid protests from multiple ethnic groups
  • Meitei and Naga civil-society groups demanded an NRC update before any census; Kuki-Zo groups took the opposite position
  • The Manipur High Court had also halted the process pending further notice

The Centre has deferred census operations in Manipur after Union Home Minister Amit Shah chaired a review meeting, putting the proposed September 1 house-listing exercise on hold amid competing demands from the state's fractured ethnic communities.

Why the Census Was Deferred

Civil-society groups from the Meitei and Naga communities had demanded that the National Register of Citizens be updated before any census operations could proceed, according to NDTV. Their concern centers on the allegation that illegal immigrants have altered the demographic composition of certain districts, and that a census conducted without an NRC update would institutionalize these changes.

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2094410990280732950

The Kuki-Zo Council took the opposite position, arguing that census operations should proceed as planned. The conflicting demands reflect the deep ethnic fault lines that have defined Manipur's politics since the Meitei-Kuki violence that erupted in May 2023 and the more recent Naga-Kuki clashes that began in February 2026.

Legal Intervention

Adding to the political complexity, the Manipur High Court had issued an order halting the census process pending further notice. The court's intervention followed petitions from civil-society groups who argued that proceeding with the census in the current security environment would be impractical and politically inflammatory.

National Census Context

India's national census, originally scheduled for 2021, has been repeatedly postponed, first due to the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequently for administrative reasons. The Manipur-specific deferral adds another layer to the delays. Census data is foundational for constituency delimitation, welfare programme targeting and infrastructure planning, making the continued postponement a governance concern.

What's Next

The Centre has not announced a revised timeline for the house-listing exercise in Manipur. The deferral is likely to remain in place until the security situation stabilizes and some consensus emerges among the state's major ethnic groups on the NRC question. For the Indian diaspora, particularly those from Manipur, the census deferral is another sign of the protracted institutional paralysis affecting the state.
nri_angle: Diaspora members from Manipur face continued uncertainty as institutional governance stalls in the state.
